summary: Forest Service 42-ft tower with R2 cab on the San Juan NF, Dolores County, CO; built 1970 to replace Glade Mountain; standing and staffed in fire season, with a locked gate on Road 26.

facts.design: R2 flattop 14 x 14 ft cab with catwalk on a 42-ft tower (wood per the register and a 2009-era account; steel per a third-party guide)

staffing.status: staffed in fire season by lookout Rick Freimuth and his wife Linda, who lived in the tower; the register notes a current lookout as of 2019

access.note: Vehicle access ends at a locked gate; the register places it 0.3 mile below the tower, a third-party guide places it just below the tower. The tower is a working fire-detection site.

visit.trail_note: Unpaved Road 26 climbs about 3.9 miles from County Road 27 (728 ft rise); snow usually blocks it October to June, per a third-party guide. The guide warns of thunderstorm exposure on the ridge. The sources read do not state public visiting rules.

events.note: Built in 1970 to replace Glade Mountain Lookout; the 42-ft tower with a 14 x 14 flat roof cab
Narraguinnep Fire, August 2009: a cabin and the Benchmark lookout were evacuated; no structure damage reported in the account read
Cab vandalized before the 2018 fire season; district installed a locked gate about 0.3 mile below the tower, plus chain-link fencing and a gate at the foot of the stairs
Catwalk railing and bracing replaced and painted; most of the east catwalk deck replaced; window frames and trim painted; two original signs restored
Solar batteries being replaced with sealed gel batteries for the 2019 season (register)
Rick and Linda Freimuth had lived in the tower for three years during fire season; Rick had made 74 smoke reports since 2018 (2020 article in The Journal; the tower's 50th anniversary year)
Three new 190W solar panels on the roof and an AXIS camera for remote use by Dolores RD fire staff, as of 2021

Per the 2022 condition report: 55 stair treads replaced with Douglas fir treads, traction tape added; new cab door replacing the one vandalized in 2018. The report says 'last summer' with no year given, so the year is the report year.
Great American Outdoors Act line item for San Juan NF Dolores RD lists Benchmark Fire Lookout Tower for renovation (planned, per the 2022 report)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register describes a wooden tower and the Forest Lookouts account says timber. A third-party 4WD guide calls the current tower steel. The story reports the disagreement.

The register, quoting the lookout's own 2019 information, puts the locked gate 0.3 mile below the tower. The Dangerous Roads guide puts it just below the tower. Both are reported; neither is official.

notes_for_editor: Brief's 2022 entries for the cab door and stair treads: the 2022 report gives no year ('last summer'), so the event year is the report year. Brief's 2021 solar date is supported ('As of 2021'). Staffing is as of the 2020 article; current staffing unknown. Material (wood vs steel) and gate location disagree across sources and are flagged, not resolved. The Dangerous Roads guide is third-party; confirm the gate and winter closure with the Dolores Ranger District. Pages read: 6 (NHLR, Forest Lookouts, the 2022 PDF with two greps, the Journal article, Dangerous Roads). Searches: 1. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the register puts the gate 0.3 mile below the tower and the story now says so; the 2019 batteries were being replaced and the story now says so; the 2020 article is dated only by its 50th-anniversary reference, so the JSON no longer gives a month.
